name: KE Holdings Inc.
sector: Real Estate / Housing transaction platform & services (China)
moat_justification: Beike/Lianjia is China's dominant integrated online-offline housing platform: the ACN agent-cooperation network, the largest verified listing database, the Lianjia brand and ~60k-store / ~540k-agent scale (Q2 2026 release) create real network effects and data advantages rivals cannot quickly replicate. But the moat is narrow-to-moderate, not wide: demand is hostage to China's housing cycle and policy, agents and consumers can multi-home, take rates face regulatory and developer pressure, and the newer renovation/rental lines carry structurally lower margins — earnings power has swung from strong profits to a negative-OE year within the last 3 fiscal years.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2023, 2024, 2025 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base

FX_CONVERTED: reporting currency CNY converted to USD at period-end ECB reference rates (frankfurter.app) — flow facts use the period-end rate, not a period average; the rates used are recorded in dcf_numbers.json fx_conversion
USD_TRANSLATIONS_USED: the issuer files its own USD convenience translations alongside its reporting currency; the engine used the filed USD figures

ADS_RATIO_APPLIED: 20-F filer — per-share figures scaled x3.0 ordinary shares per ADS (KE Holdings Inc. Form 20-F, Exhibit 2.5 (Description of Rights of Each Class of Securities Registered under Section 12, filed on EDGAR for CIK 1809587 with the annual report on Form 20-F): American Depositary Shares, each representing three Class A ordinary shares of KE Holdings Inc., listed on the NYSE; the same 1:3 ratio is restated in the company's 2026 SEC filings) so they are comparable to the ADS price; TTM pins are taken as per-ADS already
SECTOR_MODEL_MISMATCH: Finance sector — OE/capex DCF fits finance names poorly; grade confidence low
BASE_DIVERGENCE: latest FY OE/share -0.36 vs 3-yr median 0.66 — one of them is distorted; find out which and why
WIDE_SCENARIO_SPREAD: super-bull IV is 4.8x super-bear IV — uncertainty is huge; confidence should not be high
one_liner: China's dominant housing-transaction platform (Beike/Lianjia), moat 6/10 — Tier D: weighted IRR 7.20%, weighted IV@15% $6.39/ADS vs $17.83 price; even the super-bull scenario (12.54% IRR) fails the 15% hurdle, and FY2025 owner's earnings went negative on a working-capital-driven OCF collapse. Clears 15% only at or below ~$6.39/ADS.
moat_for: ACN agent-cooperation network: shared listings/commission splits across ~60k stores and ~540k agents (Q2 2026) — scale rivals cannot quickly replicate
Largest verified housing listing database + Lianjia brand trust in a fraud-prone resale market
Data/AI tooling and transaction infrastructure (VR tours, escrow, closing services) raise agent productivity and platform stickiness
Dominant share of existing-home transactions in tier-1/2 cities; existing-home GTV grew +8.0% YoY in Q2 2026 even in a weak market
moat_against: Earnings hostage to China's housing cycle and housing policy — FY2025 operating cash flow went negative
Agents and consumers can multi-home; competing platforms and developer direct-sales channels pressure take rates
New-home segment tied to distressed developer volumes (Q1 2026 new-home GTV -37.2% YoY)
Growth lines (renovation, rental) are lower-margin and working-capital heavier than the core brokerage platform
China/VIE/ADS regulatory overhang and Class B weighted-voting governance concentration
